text:
Lahaina Homecoming event to welcome back 103 former residents July 17-19
Lahaina Homecoming, a three-day community celebration focused on healing and reconnection, will take place July 17-19 at several locations in Lahaina. The event is designed to welcome home 103 former Lahaina residents and invite the public to honor the town’s enduring spirit.
“The inaugural Lahaina Homecoming represents a crucial investment in the belief that although many families have been displaced, Lahaina remains their home,” said Maui Economic Recovery Commission Chairman Layne Silva. “The event welcomes former residents and the community at large to take part in cultural experiences, storytelling, resource sharing and community-focused programming that honors Lahaina’s rich heritage and strengthens connections among residents, families and supporters as Lahaina continues its recovery.”
The initiative is led by the Maui Economic Recovery Commission’s Healing Journey Team and coordinated by nonprofit Festivals of Aloha. It is sponsored by the County of Maui Office of Recovery, Hawaiian Council, Hawaiʻi Community Foundation, Hawaiian Airlines, other local organizations, and private donors. Mayor Richard Bissen said Lahaina Homecoming reflects ongoing efforts toward healing while providing opportunities for families and friends to reconnect. “Recovery is about more than rebuilding homes and businesses. It’s about restoring the connections that make Lahaina such a special place,” Bissen said. “Lahaina Homecoming celebrates our community, welcomes families back home and reminds everyone that Lahaina's spirit remains strong.”
Events will be held at Campbell Park, Lahaina Cannery Mall, and Lahaina United Methodist Church with live entertainment, local food vendors, cultural demonstrations, career opportunities, resources for attendees, and family-friendly activities. All events are free to attend.
A key feature of this year’s event is the E Hoʻi Mai Competition, which invited former residents from across the continental United States to submit videos explaining their ties to Lahaina. Organizers initially planned airfare sponsorships for 80 people but expanded support after receiving additional applications; ultimately 103 individuals representing 20 families will return for the weekend thanks in part to Hawaiian Airlines’ contribution.
Daryl Fujiwara of Festivals of Aloha said: “Every application reminded us that Lahaina isn't just a place; it's family... Our goal was to bring home 80 people but every story reflected genuine connections to our community. We simply couldn't say no.” Trilogy Excursions will offer complimentary cruises for returning participants during the weekend.
